title: Fixed-Width Increment in Constant Space
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean word $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the fixed-width increment of $x$, using the empty word when incrementing overflows. For every Boolean word $x$ and every time $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the computation of $M$ from its initial configuration on $x$ uses at most $c$ work-tape cells through step $t$.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a finite Turing machine over Booleans
Existence of a natural-number constant c
Computes the specified increment-or-empty function within c(|x|+1) steps on every input
For every input and every t, space through step t is at most c
